## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:reports` · `pm:queue`. The fix lands on both sides: objectui registers a `ref:dataset` widget (this card), then objectstack's row spec declares it (objectstack-ai/objectstack#21714)

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-04T09:54Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Measured now, as this card's direction asked** (objectui `origin/main` `278d2444ee`):
- **`RepeaterField` honours a row field's `widget` and `required`.** The grid cell (`SchemaForm.tsx` about `:2797`–`:2810`) passes `required={Boolean(s.required)}` and `resolveFieldWidget({ …, fieldSpec: s, … })`, and the card layout does the same. So the row spec in objectstack's `report.form.ts` decides the cell.
- **`ref:dataset` has no renderer.** `widgets.tsx` `WIDGETS` registers `ref:object` and `ref:component` only (about `:2935`). An unregistered hint resolves to the raw-JSON face (`SchemaForm.tsx` about `:870`).
- **The top-level dataset picker is the inspector's curated `InspectorSelectField`** over `datasetPickerOptions`, not a spec-form widget. That is why the spec's existing top-level `widget: 'ref:dataset'` (`report.form.ts:39`) has never rendered.

**So neither side alone fixes this:**
- the row spec alone would turn the cell into a raw-JSON editor;
- the widget alone is inert until a row declares it.

**Why p2.** The producer is named and shipped. #21702's refusal (PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#21712) makes a freshly added block invalid at the next spec bump, and today such a block draws nothing.

**This card (objectui):** register `ref:dataset` in `WIDGETS`, fed by the same dataset catalog the inspector already reads.
- **Options:** `datasetPickerOptions`, the author's label and description per objectui#11161.
- **The value written is the dataset name.**
- It must work in a section and in a repeater row, in both the grid and card layouts.
- ⛔ No inspector-local override of the row. The spec row is the one authority for the control.

**The objectstack half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#21714.** The "Joined blocks" row declares `widget: 'ref:dataset'` and `required: true`. It is blocked on this card reaching objectstack's `.objectui-sha`, the install face.

**Pins:**
- a spec-form field declaring `widget: 'ref:dataset'` renders the dataset picker in a section and in a repeater row (grid and card), and writes the dataset name;
- with no catalog, it degrades to a labelled text input, not the raw-JSON face.

The widget offers `datasetPickerOptions` (`inspectors/ReportDefaultInspector.tsx:210`, the author's label and description per objectui#11161) and writes the dataset name. With no catalog it degrades to a labelled text input, not the raw-JSON face.
- Wherever the dataset catalog has to reach the widget, through `WidgetContext` or the `SchemaForm` host the report inspector already feeds; the dev measures which. `SchemaForm.tsx` is only edited if the repeater path needs it, and then named.
- New pins: the picker in a section and in a repeater row, in both grid and card layouts; the dataset name written; and the no-catalog degrade. One `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch` changeset.
- ⛔ No inspector-local override of the "Joined blocks" row: the spec row stays the one authority (triage). ⛔ No objectstack edit: the row-spec half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#21714.

The dev stops on a breach and explains it in the report.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (default judgment tier; `dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui` printed "no path-derived mandate" for `widgets.tsx` and `ReportDefaultInspector.tsx`)
Clause-②: no
Why: `WIDGETS` and `WidgetContext` are not re-exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, whose metadata-admin exports are the four page components. `ref:dataset` is already a declared hint: the spec's report form uses it at the top level, `report.form.ts:39`. Registering its renderer delivers a declared value; it widens no accept set. If a new export of the package index turns out to be needed, the dev writes `yes` and says why.
Thread-read: 5978719353
Serial constraints cleared: read 2026-10-04T10:29Z.
- **objectui#10202** (`hotlong`) claims `views/metadata-admin/**` for the Studio picklist page. Its branch `claude/issue-10202-studio-picklist` (`da4c629`) touches neither `widgets.tsx` nor `ReportDefaultInspector.tsx`. This card needs `widgets.tsx`, so it is named here.
- **This seat's in flight:** objectui#11002 (`runtime-config.ts`, `console/ConsoleShell.tsx`, the storage and read-rate hooks and banners) and, claimed in this act, objectui#11605 (the plugin registrations). Both are disjoint by file.
- **Open PRs:** objectui#11607 (objectui#8347) and #11069 touch neither file.

## Seat review of PR objectui#11611 at head `9ebe77bf9` (dev report `5979374160`): content ACCEPT. The dev measured `Clause-②: yes`, correcting this seat's claim, so the at-tier contract review runs before ready

`domain:ui` seat 1 · `session_01FjqrwXPfSMkSfkKYDSRkN2` · 2026-10-04T11:18Z. Reviewed against GitHub, not the report.

- **The seat's error, owned.** My claim `5979035511` declared `Clause-②: no`. Its reason was that `WIDGETS` and `WidgetContext` are not re-exported from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`. That reason is false: the index has `export { SchemaForm } from './views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.js';` (`:382` on `main` `b92329c`), and `SchemaForm`'s `widgetContext?: WidgetContext` prop carries `WidgetContext` onto the published type surface. The dev measured it on the built `dist`, and the seat re-read the line on `main`. The new optional member `datasets` therefore widens a published type: `yes (widening)`, `minor`. This is the second time this round that the seat's Clause-② call was wrong (after objectui#11569's patch-with-yes). The claim's export check has to follow prop types reachable from re-exported components, not only the names re-exported.
- **Shape:**
  - draft, base `main`;
  - the first line is `Fixes #11601`, with no other closing keyword. Line 2 opens `Clause-②: yes (widening).` at line start, and the measurement follows on the same line;
  - 9 files, +555 / −23. `check-governed-merges --pr objectstack-ai/objectui#11611`: NOT governed;
  - the PR assignee is `os-zhuang`, read back;
  - the changeset is `'@object-ui/app-shell': minor`.
- **Triage `5978719353`, carried out:**
  - `ref:dataset` is registered in `WIDGETS` as `RefDatasetWidget`, with its `WIDGET_LABELLING` row (`'control'`).
  - Options come from the objectui#11161 author text (`LABEL (name) — description`), and the value written is the dataset NAME.
  - Its four arms follow `RefObjectWidget`'s:
    - failed load: the shared failure notice beside an editable box;
    - loading: the stored name, disabled;
    - idle or empty catalog: a labelled text input, ⛔ never the raw-JSON face;
    - loaded: the picker, with an out-of-catalog stored name kept and flagged `(not found)`.
  - No inspector-local override of the "Joined blocks" row.
- **The catalog path:**
  - `datasetPickerOptions` and `labelBesideName` move unchanged to a pure module, `inspectors/dataset-picker-options.ts`. Importing them from the inspector would close a cycle: inspector → `SchemaForm` → widgets.
  - `ReportDefaultInspector` re-exports `datasetPickerOptions`, so `DashboardWidgetInspector` is untouched, and there is one definition.
  - The inspector now hands its existing `useDatasetCatalog` result to the spec form as `widgetContext.datasets`. It passes `conditionScope: 'none'`, the `report` row of the ruled table. The dev measured 0 predicate-named keys among the bundled `ReportSchema`'s 73 property paths, so no field this form renders changes.
  - Every other `SchemaForm` host leaves `datasets` absent, which renders the degrade.
- **`SchemaForm.tsx` is not edited:** both repeater layouts already route a row's `widget`, and the pins prove it.
- **Pins:**
  - **Red first:** at `b92329c`, the new `SchemaForm.refDatasetWidget-11601` file failed 9 of 9, each case on the raw-JSON face.
  - **Green:** at `b58a18b`, 389 files and 4,550 tests pass, selected by import and by source-text read: the metadata-admin directory, the report readers, and the `widgets.tsx` / `SchemaForm.tsx` ratchets. They were re-run at `9ebe77b`, which changes only the changeset.
  - **Ablations,** each restored by blob hash:
    - deleting the `WIDGETS` line turns 17 red, including the registry gates;
    - deleting `datasets` from the inspector's context turns both inspector picker pins red, while the 9 `SchemaForm` pins, including the degrade, stay green.
  - Three registry pins (`widgetLabelling`, 9889 grid naming, 9931 failure arm) each gain a `ref:dataset` row. They derive their population from `WIDGET_LABELLING`, so the row is owed.
- **The joined-block symptom is not closed by this PR alone.** The block row stays free text until objectstack-ai/objectstack#21714 declares `widget: 'ref:dataset'` and that spec reaches objectui. The PR body and the changeset both say so. objectstack-ai/objectstack#21714 waits on this PR reaching objectstack's `.objectui-sha`.
- **Out-of-scope:** `RowCell` (master-detail) special-cases only `ref:object` / `ref:component`, so a `ref:dataset` column inside a master-detail widget would not get the picker. No producer declares that shape, so it has zero pull ⇒ Acceptance notes.
- ⇒ `needs:contract-review` goes on the PR now, and an isolated at-tier review runs on this head. CI was in progress at this read (14 running, 0 failed).
